note: Current Arabic is understandable but awkward for 'so many people to be here'; use a direct standard construction.
proposed_target: لم أتوقع وجود هذا العدد الكبير من الناس هنا.
proposed_english: I didn't expect so many people to be here.

note: Arabic means 'I don't love anyone as much as I love you'; English 'more than' is not strictly equivalent.
proposed_target: لا أحب أحدًا بقدر ما أحبك.
proposed_english: I don't love anyone as much as I love you.

note: English adds 'exactly', which is absent from Arabic; use an uncontracted direct equivalent that preserves C-band progression.
proposed_target: لا أتذكّر أين وضعت مفاتيحي.
proposed_english: I do not remember where I put the keys.

note: Arabic directly says 'I don't see a problem'; use the direct English equivalent.
proposed_target: لا أرى مشكلة فيما تفعل.
proposed_english: I don't see a problem with what you're doing.

note: أقطع وعدًا is an unnatural calque; use أتعهد and an English pledge construction that stays in the audited C-band.
proposed_target: أتعهد بأنني سأقلع عن التدخين.
proposed_english: I make a pledge that I will quit smoking.

note: إلا is the wrong connective here; English also says they 'seem' to love the speaker.
proposed_target: أكره البعوض جدًا، لكن يبدو أنهم يحبونني جدًا.
proposed_english: I hate mosquitoes, but they seem to love me.

note: مسبقًا means in advance; align English directly and naturally.
proposed_target: كان عليّ أن أحجز في الفندق مسبقًا.
proposed_english: I should have made a hotel reservation in advance.

note: Multiple missing hamzas/orthographic issues and smoother past-progressive match are needed.
proposed_target: خرجت مسرعًا لأرى ماذا كان يحدث في الخارج.
proposed_english: I rushed out to see what was going on.

note: Missing initial hamza in أقترح.
proposed_target: أقترح عليك الكفّ عن طرح الكثير من الأسئلة السخيفة.
proposed_english: I suggest you stop asking so many stupid questions.

note: Arabic مساحة كبيرة means 'a lot of space', not necessarily excessive 'too much'.
proposed_target: أعتقد أن هذه الطاولة تأخذ مساحة كبيرة.
proposed_english: I think this table takes up a lot of space.

note: Normalize tanwin and punctuation.
proposed_target: أريد أن أكون طيارًا في المستقبل.
proposed_english: I want to be a pilot in the future.

note: Severe number mismatch: Arabic says thirty, English says thirteen.
proposed_target: كنت أبلغ الثلاثين عامًا فقط آنذاك.
proposed_english: I was only thirty years old at that time.

note: Arabic addresses 'you' (تتوقف); English incorrectly says 'she'.
proposed_target: أتمنى أن تتوقف عن تشغيل تلك الموسيقى الغبية.
proposed_english: I wish you would stop playing that stupid music.

note: Standard orthography uses غدًا.
proposed_target: سأتواصل معك عبر الهاتف غدًا.
proposed_english: I'll get in touch with you by phone tomorrow.

note: بأقرب وقت is a calque; standard expression is في أقرب وقت ممكن.
proposed_target: سأعيد الكتاب في أقرب وقت ممكن.
proposed_english: I'll return the book as soon as I can.

note: Arabic says 'to a safe place'; use a natural future equivalent that remains in the audited C-band.
proposed_target: سآخذك إلى مكان آمن.
proposed_english: I am going to take you to a safe place.

note: أتتطلع is a typo; correct form is أتطلع.
proposed_target: أنا أتطلع لقضاء وقت مع أسرتي.
proposed_english: I'm looking forward to spending time with my family.

note: Current word order is awkward; use the standard مما إذا construction.
proposed_target: لست متأكدًا حتى مما إذا كان هذا مفتاحي.
proposed_english: I'm not even sure if this is my key.

note: مخرّب بالكامل means completely run-down/ruined; use a natural equivalent long enough to preserve the audited C-band.
proposed_target: يبدو هذا المنزل مخرّبًا بالكامل.
proposed_english: It looks as though this house is completely run-down.

note: لنعمل حفلة is an unnatural calque; use لنقم بحفلة.
proposed_target: لنقم بحفلة شاي بعد غد.
proposed_english: Let's have a tea party the day after tomorrow.

note: Arabic says a new car, not specifically 'my new car'.
proposed_target: زوجتي خائفة من قيادة سيارة جديدة.
proposed_english: My wife is afraid to drive a new car.

note: Standard spelling is إبلاغي.
proposed_target: الرجاء إبلاغي عن أي تغيير في حالته.
proposed_english: Please inform me of any change in his condition.

note: توقف المطر means the rain has stopped; express يمكننا as ability without losing C-band progression.
proposed_target: لقد توقف المطر، لذا يمكننا البدء.
proposed_english: The rain has stopped, so we are able to begin.
